title: Hash Maps & Sets: Fast Lookups Explained

scenes.line1: Why are hash maps and sets so fast?
scenes.say: Hash maps and sets are interview favorites. Why are they so fast, and how do they handle collisions?

scenes.label: HashMap
scenes.sub: Stores key-value pairs with O(1) average lookup.
scenes.say: Hash maps store key-value pairs and offer constant time lookup, insert, and delete.

scenes.label: Set
scenes.sub: Keeps unique elements with O(1) operations.
scenes.say: Sets keep unique elements, also with fast operations.
When two keys hash to the same bucket, that's a collision. We handle it with chaining or open addressing.
Python dictionaries use hash maps. Insert, check, and retrieve values in constant time.

scenes.question: How do you handle hash map collisions?
scenes.right: Use chaining or open addressing to store colliding keys.
scenes.say: In interviews, don't ignore collisions. Mention chaining or open addressing as solutions.
